output.summary: The vendor's SLA fails both user constraints. First, scheduled maintenance allows up to 8 hours (2 hours/week * 4 weeks) of downtime during US business hours, which exceeds the 60-minute monthly limit. Second, the service credit cap is 10% of the monthly fee, which is significantly below the required 50% reimbursement threshold for SLA breaches. Both critical constraints are violated.
key_claims: Scheduled maintenance allows up to 8 hours of downtime per month during business hours
Service credit is capped at 10% of the monthly fee
risks_or_flaws: Scheduled maintenance exclusion (up to 8 hours/month) exceeds the 60-minute maximum permitted outage constraint
Service credit cap (10%) is less than the required 50% reimbursement threshold
output.verification_question: Can the vendor reduce scheduled maintenance windows to under 60 minutes total per month and increase the service credit to at least 50% of the monthly fee?
